[...] While "across" and "cross" share etymological roots and touch upon the concept of traversing or intersecting, they diverge in their specific meanings, spatial implications, and symbolic connotations. "Across" pertains to moving horizontally or overcoming obstacles, while "cross" signifies intersecting, connecting, and crossing boundaries. sources.snippet:
> coats across the bed; straddled across the boundary line.

## adverb

1. from one side to another.
2. on the other side.

   > We'll soon be across.
3. crosswise; transversely.

   > with arms across.
4. so as to be understood or learned.

   > He couldn't get the idea across to the class.
5. into a desired or successful state.

   > to put a business deal across.

## adjective

1. being in a crossed or transverse position; crosswise.
